newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Strength in British ADRs, Israel weak.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Strength in British ADRs, Israel weak.

text.p: British stocks traded in New York saw a smattering of strength on Monday afternoon while Israeli issues were mostly depressed despite U.S. efforts to organize an emergency Middle East summit.
Analysts also said there was interest in Latin American shares but it was not translating so far today into volume or price moves.
"Things are very unsettled in the Middle East and they will remain unsettled until the summit actually occurs," said Robert Gay, managing director at Bankers Trust.
Among British shares putting in a firm showing was LucasVarity Plc LV.N, which was up 1-3/4 at 39-5/8 on the NYSE after brokerage Kleinwort Benson reiterated a buy recommendation on the stock.
"There's a buy note and people are interested at these lower levels," a trader in London said.

British Airways was up 1-7/8 at 85-1/8 while Imperial Chemical Industries Plc was up 1-3/8 at 53 and Zeneca Group was up one at 74-1/4 after Prudential Securities was reported to have initiated coverage of it with a buy rating.

Israeli stocks traded in the United States were mostly fractionally lower despite Washington's efforts to organize a summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat after bloody clashes in which almost 70 people were killed.
Only Teledata Communications Ltd was up one at 18-1/2.
Gay said that while there was interest in Latin American shares today, it was not translating into buying or high volume.

"There is a lot of interest in Latin America because of the new issues in Argentina and Brazil and the implications for debt buyback," Gay said. "It's not showing up in the performance of the ADRs. It forms the background for ADRs."
